name: Optery
summary: Personal data removal service that scans people-search sites and data brokers for your name and address and files opt-out requests, from a free self-service report to managed removals with a human agent.
best_for: people in the US who want their home address and phone number off people-search sites, from a free self-service scan up to a managed service with a human agent
skip_if: you only have one current address and are willing to file opt-outs yourself with the free report, or you need protection outside the countries Optery serves
honest_knock: Core automates removals for one name and one city and state only, with no human handling exceptions; past addresses and name variations need Extended at $12.42 a month yearly. The advertised site counts assume Expanded Reach is enabled; without it Core covers 150+ sites instead of 375+ (13 November 2026). Custom removal requests on Ultimate only start after 30 days. Removals from data brokers take time and listings can reappear, which is why every paid plan rescans monthly. Personal plans are only for residents of the United States, Canada (excluding Quebec), Australia, New Zealand and South Africa (help desk, updated 25 September 2026). Optery does not remove anything from social media, forums, blogs, news sites, legal-records sites or documents posted online, and offers no dark-web scanning. Cancelling stops future billing, keeps the plan until the end of the paid term and then drops the account to Free Basic, with no pro-rated refund outside the 30-day guarantee.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Core · per month billed yearly ($39 a year)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-10 on optery.com/pricing, US view, USD, monthly and yearly figures; re-read 2026-10-24 with a plain fetch: prices, the 17% yearly saving and the FALL2026 banner unchanged, site counts on Extended and Ultimate slightly lower, as noted below) Optery sells personal data-broker removal in four tiers. Free Basic costs nothing and needs no card: a personalised exposure report with screenshots, a scan of your Google and Bing results, and self-service removal tools, but no automated removals. Core is $3.99 a month, or $3.25 a month billed yearly ($39 a year): automated monthly removals from 380+ sites (150+ without enabling Expanded Reach), for at most one name and one city and state per user, fully automated with no human Privacy Agent. Extended is $14.99 a month, or $12.42 billed yearly ($149): 555+ sites (330+ without Expanded Reach; 325+ on 10 October), unlimited name variations and past cities, an assigned human Privacy Agent, removal reports with before-and-after screenshots about every 90 days, and blurring your home on Google Maps and Apple Maps. Ultimate, marked most popular, is $24.99 a month, or $20.70 billed yearly ($249): 625+ sites (400+ without Expanded Reach; 630+ and 405+ on 10 October), unlimited custom removal requests across 940+ sites (945+ on 10 October) once you have been a customer for 30 days, outdated-content removal submissions to Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo and Yahoo, and priority email support. Yearly billing saves 17%. Individual accounts have a 'No Questions Asked' 30-day money-back guarantee. On that reading a site banner offered promo code FALL2026 for 20% off at checkout, with no end date shown. Family plans are not priced on the pricing page: Optery's help desk (updated 19 October 2026) says one family plan can cover as many people as you like, each with their own Optery account, with a discount that grows with the number of people up to 30% off paid plans, and that promo codes cannot be applied to family plans. Business plans are priced on a separate page that we did not read for this review. A plain fetch of optery.com/pricing on 13 November 2026 returned the plan feature lists but not the amounts, which load by script, so the prices were not re-read that day. The site counts were lower again: Core 375+ (150+ without Expanded Reach), Extended 550+ (325+), Ultimate 620+ (395+), and custom removal requests across 935+ sites. The page notes that the 30-day money-back guarantee applies to individual (consumer) accounts only and not to business accounts.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Optery in an existing Free Basic our account without entering personal data: the dashboard with its coverage of 0 / 621 data brokers and the list of 396 sites, the plan page on the Monthly and Yearly tabs, the countries in the help article, the cancel and pause text in the FAQ and the place of the Delete Account button. The scan was not run because it needs real personal data, and the checkout was not reached. Nothing was paid and nothing was changed. Start and account: the test started at 16:15 (Dutch time) in the existing Optery our account on the Free Basic plan, already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English (only the cookie bar was in Dutch and it was not confirmed). The hard limit of the test was that no personal data was entered, no scan was started and nothing was changed. The dashboard opened about 15 seconds after the address was loaded (16:16:13 to 16:16:28), after an empty first screen, in 1 step. Onboarding: the button 4 / 4 What to do next lists the Onboarding tasks: look at the screenshots and View links, upgrade for removals (the app says removal of profiles starts in 1 - 3 business days), Update your Profile (the more info, the better) and Share Optery. The profile form was only read for its labels and nothing was typed: the tabs Basic Info, Emails, Phones, Addresses, Addt'l Info, Relatives, Power of Attorney and Safety Program; in Basic Info the fields First Name, Last Name, Middle name (recommended), Birth Year, Birth Day (recommended), Birth Month (recommended) and Gender; a reCAPTCHA stands on the page. The profile page itself was not kept as evidence because it shows a name, an e-mail address and a birth year that cannot be covered cleanly. Core action, the data broker overview and the coverage of the plan: the dashboard says Data Brokers Covered by Your FREE BASIC Plan 0 / 621. The list All Sites (396) has 8 pages of 10 and the columns WEBSITE, PLAN COVERAGE (FREE BASIC), EXPOSURE RISK, RE-EXPOSED, LINK TO PROFILE and MORE INFO; the rows read Core Upgrade for coverage and some have a View link; the tabs are PRIMARY SCAN, CUSTOM SCAN and EXPANDED REACH, and Buy Custom Scan is greyed out. The empty results area says that screenshots of exposed data appear once the vendor finds them. The list has no country column or filter (only With re-exposures and Without re-exposures). The scan was NOT tested, because it needs real personal data. The dashboard also showed Your scan is about to start with a countdown of 35 minutes, the advice to complete the profile first and the buttons Postpone Scan by 45 mins and Scan Now: the scan starts by itself with the profile that already exists in the account. We did not postpone it and did not start it. Countries: the help article of 09/25/2026 says Optery is available to residents of the United States, Canada (excluding Quebec), Australia, New Zealand and South Africa at this time; other countries can make an account and are told when their country is supported; business customers on enterprise plans can cover non-U.S. residents. The Netherlands and the rest of Europe are not served for private persons. The footer has a link Pricing - Canada. Plans: Free Basic lists a Personalized Exposure Report with Screenshots, a Custom Scan of Your Google Search Results, Self-Service Removal Tools, a Phone and Email Scan Preferences Tool, Profile Visibility at Hundreds of Sites with Patented View Links, Unlimited Name Variations (for the same person), Unlimited Past Cities and States and standard e-mail help. Yearly: Core $3.25 a month ($39.00 billed yearly, automated removal from 377+ sites), Extended $12.42 ($149.00 billed yearly, 554+ sites) and Ultimate $20.75 ($249.00 billed yearly, 623+ sites, MOST POPULAR); the page says Save 17%, which ~ 2 free months. Monthly: Core $3.99, Extended $14.99 and Ultimate $24.99. Core: automated removals from 377+ sites (or 152+ without enabling Expanded Reach), with a maximum of 1 name and city and state per user, monthly automated scans and removals and a Bot Only approach with no human Privacy Agent for QA or special cases. Extended: 554+ sites (or 329+), unlimited name variations, unlimited past cities and states, a Humans and Machines approach with an assigned human Privacy Agent and removal reports with before and after screenshots about every 90 days. Ultimate: 623+ sites (or 398+), Unlimited Custom Removal Requests for 1,360+ sites total (eligible after 30 days), the Google and Bing outdated content tool and priority e-mail help. The refund text says to cancel the account within 30 days of the first purchase and then send the refund request to the vendor help address, to be processed within 5 - 10 business days. The Account page says AI Model Preferences (Internal (default) or External (OpenAI)) and Maps Preferences need Extended or Ultimate. Differences with the dossier: the Ultimate yearly price is $20.75 in the app (249 divided by 12) where the dossier has $20.70; the site counts in the app are 377+, 554+ and 623+ (152+, 329+ and 398+ without Expanded Reach) where the dossier has slightly different numbers; the custom removals are 1,360+ sites in the app where the dossier has 940+; the dashboard names 621 data brokers in the coverage box and 396 sites in the list; Free Basic also lists Unlimited Name Variations and Unlimited Past Cities and States, and the Google scan on Free Basic is a Google Search Results scan. Checkout: NOT reached. No payment method was added (the Account page says no payment methods have been added yet) and Upgrade was not clicked, so no total, tax or renewal term was seen. Cancelling: the FAQ on the Plans page says a paid plan can be paused through Pause Subscription on the Account page, and cancelled by downgrading to Free Basic from the Plans page or through the button Cancel Subscription on the Account page, after which billing stops and the plan stays active for the rest of the paid period (the end of the text was cut off). The Free Basic account has no Cancel Subscription button, so no cancellation was seen. The Account page has a section Delete Account: This will permanently delete your Optery account, you lose your optout progress and profile info and there is no turning back, with a red button Permanently Delete My Optery Account that was not clicked. Not covered by the service (FAQ): blogs, news, forums, social media (LinkedIn, Facebook, TikTok and others), legal registers, documents online and the dark web. Not tested: the scan, filling the profile, the exposure report with screenshots, the Custom Scan, Expanded Reach and the power of attorney, real removals and the time until a listing is gone, a paid plan, the checkout page, Cancel Subscription, the family plan, the business plan and the mobile app. Clean up: the account, the profile and the plan (Free Basic) were left unchanged and the cookie bar was not confirmed. The hiding of the name and the avatar on the dashboard was done only temporarily in the page and nothing was saved. All our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The scan starts by itself after a countdown with the profile that exists in the account, Core covers one name and one city and state only, the site counts in the app differ from the dossier and the dashboard names 621 brokers where the list has 396 sites, private accounts exist only in five countries, the Free Basic account has no cancel button so the cancellation route stays unseen, the end of the cancellation text was cut off in the FAQ, and the scan result and the removals could not be tested without personal data.
